title: The Shanghai Times, Wednesday November 1, 1922

（印：3/22）

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, WEDNESDAY, NOVEMBER 1, 1922.

Escape Of Siberian Fleet
Tokyo, Oct. 30.
A "Jiji" special telegram from
Seishin, Chosen, dated October
30 states:—Thirteen warships of
the Siberian Fleet, which have
escaped from Vladivostok, ar-
rived at the port of Seishin on
October 29. Admiral Stark, the
Commander of the Fleet, is, toge-
ther with his family, living on
board a warship. Major-General
Kalnikoff, the Principal of the
Military Preparatory School at
Vladivostok, accompanied by his
students, upwards of 200 in num-
ber, is also on board a warship.
The men-of-war above-mentioned
have on board some 8,000 re-
fugees, including soldiers, who
are forbidden to communicate
with the shore. The refugees,
after receiving a supply of water,
are expected to proceed to Gen-
zan and then to Harbin and
Shanghai.—Eastern News Agency.

（印：3/22）

《字林西报》，1922年11月1日，星期三。

西伯利亚舰队出逃
东京，10月30日。
据10月30日从朝鲜清津发来的《时事新报》特约电称：从符拉迪沃斯托克（海参崴）出逃的西伯利亚舰队十三艘军舰，于10月29日抵达清津港。舰队司令斯塔克海军上将与其家人同住在一艘军舰上。符拉迪沃斯托克军事预备学校校长卡尔尼科夫少将，在其两百余名学生的陪同下，也驻于一艘军舰之上。上述军舰载有约八千名难民，其中包括士兵，他们被禁止与岸上联系。难民们在获得供水后，预计将前往元山，随后转往哈尔滨和上海。——东方通讯社
